Reviewed all 49 verbs in shard 15; wrote 6 findings to `verbdata/gloss-review/shards/gloss_015.out.json`.

| Verb | Shipped | Severity | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `einkommen` | earn | high | come in (of money) |
| `einkehren` | sojourn | medium | stop at an inn |
| `einreisen` | enter, travel | medium | enter a country |
| `einschreiben` | write into, inscribe | medium | enroll, register |
| `einschulen` | instruct for a specific position, task | medium | enroll in school |
| `einschneiden` | engrave, carve | low | cut into, carve |

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Two of the six (`einschreiben`, `einschulen`) are the exact `fernschauen` shape: kaikki's sense 0 is the *literal* compositional reading (write + in, school + in) while the sense in daily use sits further down the list. Separable-prefix verbs invite this, because the compositional reading is always available to a lexicographer even when nobody uses it.
- `einschulen` adds a regional axis on top: the shipped sense is the Austrian workplace-training one. That's the same failure mode as `fernschauen` running in reverse — there the southern sense was the right one and got skipped; here it's the wrong one and got shipped.
- `einkommen` is the only defect here that no import rule could catch, since "earn" is neither truncated nor a cross-reference — it is just a transitive English verb attached to an intransitive German one. Those need a reader who tries to build a sentence with the gloss.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
